messages:
Priya (PM): proposing a new 'QoS slice' add-on for low-latency routes — goal: give customers a way to pay for prioritized inference without buying Dedicated pools. want product + pricing shape + launch criteria feedback.
Alex H: short summary of the shape pls — is this per-request, per-minute, or a % uplift on existing pricing?
Priya (PM): initial idea: per-route minute reservation + per-token surcharge during bursts. think of it like a token-bucket lease: you buy X min of high-priority routing and it applies to specific API keys/routes.
Samir (Eng): technical constraints: routing + circuit-breakers are doable, but we need rate limits per-route, tracking prefix hits, and a fast fallback to standard queue. KV caching interacts with it. estimate 2 sprints for infra + 1 sprint for console.
Emily P (Product Ops): launch criteria suggestion: 1) pilot with 2 customers, 2) p99 latency uplift <30ms for priority slices, 3) billing visibility in console and per-route usage in logs.
Todd (Finance): pricing levers: charge a base reservation per-month per-route (e.g., $X/min reserved) + per-token uplift during usage. need numbers. sales will push for discounts for pilots. also want to model revenue vs cannibalization.
Olivia (Sales): pilots: one fintech and one gaming customer asked for deterministic latency. they'd sign pilot if pricing is usage-based and not long-term commit. they want a trial window and one baseline free minute bucket.
Marta (Sales Eng): customer asks: ability to scope to specific model versions and to fall back to cheaper model automatically when slice exhausted. can we support model-variant fallback at route level?
Samir (Eng): fallback on exhaustion is straightforward: route metadata + policy engine. supporting per-model variant compatibility mapping adds complexity but doable in next phase.
Priya (PM): product tradeoffs: conservative launch supports only per-route slices (no per-model mapping). future roadmap item: 'model affinity' for slice. we should capture in requirements doc.
Todd (Finance): for pricing experiments recommend 2 shapes: A) reservation-only: monthly reservation priced per-minute with short-term refund credits for unused minutes; B) reservation + usage uplift: cheap reservation + per-token multiplier (e.g., 1.4x tokens). run both in pilot A/B.
Olivia (Sales): customers will prefer B. easier to justify lower upfront. ask for suggested numbers we can present.
Priya (PM): propose starting numbers for pilot: reservation $0.30/min (billed monthly), surge multiplier 1.5x token price during priority usage, trial grant 10k priority-mins for pilot. feedback?
Todd (Finance): run model: assume avg 10k tokens/min at 0.001/token => math looks odd. can you surface a sample spreadsheet?
Emily P (Product Ops): I'll prepare a basic spreadsheet and the scenario sims. also need per-route UI mocks for enabling slice, scoping, and a usage chart.
Samir (Eng): implementation checklist: - routing policy flag - per-route quota accounting - fast path queue - fallback policy - telemetry (p95/p99 per route) - billing export fields
Priya (PM): launch blockers: legal/contract wording for add-on (Olivia/Marta flagged), console UX, billing pipeline changes, pilot customers signed.
legal-bot: FYI — any new billing product that creates recurring charges or reservations requires review of TOS and invoice templates. submit a ticket to legal with pricing details.
Marta (Sales Eng): flagging customer ask: one regulated customer requires audit logs for when slice was used and which fallback served requests. ensure telemetry includes route-level event logs.
Samir (Eng): we can emit an audit event per request for slice decision, but volume / cost needs evaluation. maybe sampling for long-term retention.
Priya (PM): next steps: Emily to draft launch criteria + spreadsheet, Samir to scope infra story points, Todd to run revenue cannibalization sims, Olivia/Marta to line up two pilot customers, legal-bot to kick off review. sync in 48h?
Olivia (Sales): client intro calls scheduled next week, will bring proposed pricing.
Todd (Finance): I'll model the two pricing shapes and share by EOD tomorrow.
Emily P (Product Ops): I'll drop mock screenshots and the launch checklist in this thread once ready.
Priya (PM): thanks all — calling this GH:QoS-slice. If anyone has strong objections to the proposed pricing numbers, reply here. otherwise we'll move to formal PRD draft. :thumbsup:
Alex H: no objections from eng side on the approach. prioritize observability hooks early.
Samir (Eng): +1 on observability first.
Olivia (Sales): +1
Marta (Sales Eng): adding customer nuance in the PRD after Olivia's calls.
Priya (PM): closing for now — will post PRD draft in 24-48h.
